claims.text: There is a category of file with nowhere good to live: a risk register with real system names, a regulatory analysis still being argued, an agent's working memory, client material under NDA.
claims.quote: There is a category of file that has nowhere good to live.

claims.text: All of it wants what git gives, history, branches, diffs and a link, and all of it is why people say we can't put that in GitHub, so it ends up where nobody can diff it.
claims.quote: So it ends up in a shared drive, an email thread, or a Notion page nobody can diff, and the version history that mattered is gone.

claims.text: sgit is git for those files: encrypted before they leave your machine, versioned exactly like git, stored on a server that cannot read a single byte.
claims.quote: Encrypted before they leave your machine, versioned exactly like git, stored on a server that cannot read a single byte.

claims.text: sgit installs with pip install sgit-ai; it is pure Python with two runtime dependencies, under Apache-2.0.
claims.quote: Pure Python, two runtime dependencies, Apache-2.0.

claims.text: Zero knowledge, precisely: the server holds ciphertext and nothing else, not filenames, directory structure or commit messages; there is no key escrow, no admin override and no support engineer who can recover it.
claims.quote: the server holds ciphertext and nothing else.

claims.text: No key escrow and no admin override is a feature with a real cost: lose the vault key and the data is gone.
claims.quote: that last part is a feature with a real cost, which is worth being honest about up front

claims.text: The vault key, a 24-character passphrase and a vault id, is three things at once: the address of the vault, the authorisation to write to it, and the key that decrypts it.
claims.quote: the address of the vault, the authorisation to write to it, and the key that decrypts it

claims.text: A read key derives one way from the vault key, same vault, read-only, safe to publish; every vault linked from sgit.ai is published as a read key and no vault key has ever been published, enforced by a tripwire in the release pipeline.
claims.quote: a rule enforced by a tripwire in the release pipeline that scans every file before either remote is touched

claims.text: A real clone of the published EU AI Act vault yields 273 objects and 207 files, with the read key as the entire credential and no account or login.
claims.quote: A real clone of the published EU AI Act vault. 273 objects, 207 files.

value.unit: files in the EU AI Act vault

claims.text: As the machine storing it sees the same vault: 786 bytes of AES-256-GCM ciphertext, named by a SHA-256 of the encrypted bytes.
claims.quote: 786 bytes of AES-256-GCM ciphertext.

value.unit: bytes of ciphertext in one object

claims.text: Because objects are content-addressed over their ciphertext, the host can deduplicate, cache for a year and serve from a CDN while unable to tell what they are.
claims.quote: the host can deduplicate it, cache it for a year, and serve it from a CDN, while remaining unable to tell you what it is

claims.text: Underneath it is a real version control system: multi-parent commits, a tree per directory, deterministic refs derived by HMAC, merge-base computation and three-way merge, on content the server cannot interpret.
claims.quote: multi-parent commits, a tree per directory, deterministic refs derived by HMAC, a genuine merge-base computation across all parents, and three-way merge

claims.text: Nineteen published vaults are live, from a photo library to Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 parsed from official Formex XML into 1,523 nodes and 1,944 edges.
claims.quote: parsed from official Formex XML into 1,523 nodes and 1,944 edges

value.unit: nodes in the EU AI Act graph

claims.text: Before writing, all nineteen vaults were cloned from their published keys: 1,389 files, no failures.
claims.quote: Before writing this I cloned all nineteen from their published keys: 1,389 files, no failures.

claims.text: A vault can contain an application that runs against the vault without being handed a credential: with permissions set to nothing, the app renders the whole risk graph because the host reads the vault and passes results in.
claims.quote: The app never sees a key.

claims.text: Capability without credential means you can run code you did not write against data you care about, with the blast radius set by a config file you can read in one screen.
claims.quote: with the blast radius set by a config file you can read in one screen

claims.text: sgit.ai is one of nineteen sites on *.sgit.ai, each taking one question further than a section could; most of the thinking behind sgit lives out there.
claims.quote: each taking one question further than a section could

claims.text: The network includes graphs.sgit.ai, where meaning lives in the edges; risks.sgit.ai, where a risk cannot be denied, only accepted for a time; llms.sgit.ai, where an app calls a model without an API key; issues-fs; and open-source.sgit.ai.
claims.quote: A node is just a node. Meaning lives in the edges.

claims.text: The house style: each site publishes its argument before the thing exists and states what has shipped and what has not; sg-sentinel.sgit.ai says NOT BUILT at the top of every page.
claims.quote: We would rather be checkable than impressive.

claims.text: To try it, pip install and clone the EU AI Act vault: 207 files on disk in under a minute, from a key printed on a public web page, with no account anywhere; every vault also opens in the browser.
claims.quote: from a key printed on a public web page, with no account anywhere

claims.text: sgit is beta and says so on every page.
claims.quote: sgit is beta and says so on every page

claims.text: The sgit.ai site is itself served from a vault, released 59 times, each release logged in full including the ones that broke something.
claims.quote: released 59 times, and each release is logged in full, including the ones that broke something

claims.text: The article is also published as a LinkedIn newsletter post with the same argument and screenshots; it was written by Dinis Cruz and the agentic team working with him, under CC BY 4.0.
claims.quote: Written by Dinis Cruz and the agentic team working with him.
